title: Nouka Baich
summary: In the rainy season, villages of the Bengal delta send long, narrow boats down the river, each carrying a crew that paddles to the song and drum of a caller standing amidships. Whole villages line the banks to cheer.
howToPlay: Watch the ring on the pad close: strike that side the moment it meets the pad.
Alternate left and right with the caller's beat; two strokes on one side swing the boat toward the bank.
Keep the stroke clean through the rough water and round the two marker buoys, and cross the line ahead of the other boats.
Two races; your score is the average of both.
rules: Each stroke is graded by how close it falls to the beat; a stroke on the beat drives the boat, a stroke off it only tires the crew.
Striking the same side twice drifts the boat toward the bank and scrapes away speed.
Rough water narrows the timing window.
A marker buoy is passed cleanly only with a steady stroke as you reach it.
The river carries every boat gently downstream.
Three rival boats race you; the boat across the line first wins.
heritageNote: Boat races are a favourite of the rainy and early autumn months across Bangladesh and the neighbouring river country of eastern India. A caller keeps the crew in time with song and drum while the banks fill with spectators.
